_comment: Who may reach the S3 gateway, and what they may do there.
This file is mounted read-only into the seaweedfs container. A process that could
rewrite its own access control has none, and an object store holding every asset,
export and backup in the system is the wrong place to find that out.
ONE IDENTITY, AND IT IS NOT ADMIN. The application reads and writes objects; it never
needs to create or delete a bucket, because buckets are created once by provision.sh
and their number is a decision in brain.ops.storage rather than something a running
process chooses. So the actions here are Read, Write and List and deliberately not
Admin: a compromised application key can corrupt objects, which is bad and is what
versioning on the backups bucket is for, and it cannot delete the bucket they live in.
THE ANONYMOUS IDENTITY IS ABSENT ON PURPOSE. SeaweedFS grants public access by naming
an identity called 'anonymous', and every bucket in brain.ops.storage carries
public_read=False. There is no anonymous block below, so there is nothing to set to
true by accident and nothing for a reviewer to misread as disabled.
THE CREDENTIAL HERE IS A PLACEHOLDER AND MUST BE REPLACED AT DEPLOY TIME.
M32.3.1.4 issues these from OpenBao, and ops/openbao/credential-slots.md is where the
slot is described. A literal key checked into a repository is a key that has leaked,
so this value is deliberately one nothing would mistake for real.
